tier_records.rationale: CI is explicitly defined (S8) as severity(%) x host-reaction constant. FRS/TRS IS the severity(%) input to that formula. So CI is a direct, documented transform of FRS/TRS given the host reaction score — convertible, not just related, provided the reaction score is also reported.
evidence_checked: S8 abstract gives explicit formula and constants

tier_records.rationale: Both quantify rust severity but CI is a point (single-timepoint) score and AUDPC integrates severity over multiple timepoints across the season. No validated CI<->AUDPC conversion formula found in any of the 9 abstracts; every study that reports both reports them side by side, never converts one from the other.
evidence_checked: S1, S3, S4, S6, S7, S8 all report CI/ACI and AUDPC/rAUDPC as parallel, separately-computed metrics

tier_records.rationale: Seedling infection type is a categorical, race-specific greenhouse readout (controlled inoculation, single race per test) capturing qualitative gene-for-gene resistance. CI/AUDPC are continuous, field-stage, natural-infection readouts capturing quantitative slow-rusting resistance. Different growth stage, different scale type, different biological question (race-specific vs durable/partial resistance) — not mergeable even though both are commonly reported in the same paper about the same lines.
evidence_checked: S2 reports only seedling IT; S6 reports both seedling IT AND field CI/FRS/rAUDPC for an overlapping cohort, never combined into one score

tier_records.rationale: Different constructs entirely (disease severity vs. yield outcome), not just different operationalizations of the same construct — correctly excluded from pooling as the same metric family. Flagged as UNRELATED in the tiering sense (not mergeable as the same measurement) while still being causally interesting to report alongside each other. Notably only 1 of 9 studies (S8) reports this link at all — insufficient evidence to synthesize a severity->yield relationship across studies yet.
evidence_checked: Only S8 links severity metrics to yield; S1-S7, S9 stop at the disease metric
